datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) data (RHS and GTS measurements)
datasets.instrument_sensor: Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) Relative Humidity Sensor (RHS); Ground Temperature Sensor (GTS)
datasets.measurement_observable: In situ meteorology: air relative humidity (with respect to ice) at 1.6 m height; air temperature entering RHS; ground temperature/brightness temperature derived from infrared radiance
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: GTS infrared bands: 8–14 μm, 14.5–15.5 μm, 15.5–19 μm
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ time-series environmental measurements (humidity, air temperature, ground temperature)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols of MSL mission; rover landed 5 August 2012
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater floor and along Curiosity traverse; landing location given as 4.7°S, 137°E; some discussed events near active sand dunes (sols 1232 and 1311)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Nominal REMS acquisition strategy: 5 min of measurements at 1 Hz every Mars hour, with interspersed full-hour sample periods at 1 Hz; analysis used hourly values (e.g., typically 24 hourly values of RHi_a and Ta)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Updated REMS calibrations (last calibration mentioned: June 2015); additional filtering to highest-confidence measurements (e.g., first 4 s after RHS turn-on; GTS with highest recalibration quality/no shadows)
datasets.how_used: Used REMS RHS (air relative humidity and air temperature) and GTS (ground temperature via IR emission) measurements to compute simultaneous hourly ground temperature and inferred ground relative humidity, convert between RHi and RHl phase space, compare against calcium perchlorate deliquescence/efflorescence phase constraints, and derive nighttime enthalpy changes (via Clausius–Clapeyron fits) and to constrain/validate subsurface heat/mass transfer modeling.

queries.query: I need processed (physical-unit) in situ meteorology time-series from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS suite at Gale crater covering the early-to-mid mission (roughly the first 1648 sols after landing), specifically including relative humidity measured with respect to ice and the coincident air temperature plus the infrared-derived ground temperature/brightness temperature from the ground temperature sensor, suitable for constructing hourly-quality RH–T phase-space comparisons for brine stability analyses.

I need raw 1 Hz REMS records from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover at Gale crater spanning the early mission (roughly the first 1648 sols after landing) to explicitly evaluate relative humidity sensor self-heating/transients by isolating the first few seconds after each sensor turn-on, while also retaining the simultaneous ground temperature sensor measurements for time-aligned RH–T screening.

final_output.query: I need processed (physical-unit) in situ meteorology time-series from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS suite at Gale crater covering the early-to-mid mission (roughly the first 1648 sols after landing), specifically including relative humidity measured with respect to ice and the coincident air temperature plus the infrared-derived ground temperature/brightness temperature from the ground temperature sensor, suitable for constructing hourly-quality RH–T phase-space comparisons for brine stability analyses.

I need raw 1 Hz REMS records from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover at Gale crater spanning the early mission (roughly the first 1648 sols after landing) to explicitly evaluate relative humidity sensor self-heating/transients by isolating the first few seconds after each sensor turn-on, while also retaining the simultaneous ground temperature sensor measurements for time-aligned RH–T screening.
